questions.q: Which of the following is primarily a PREVENTIVE network security tool that allows or blocks traffic based on defined rules?
questions.solution: A firewall inspects incoming/outgoing traffic against allow/deny rules and blocks unauthorised connections. Antivirus reacts to malware found in files.

questions.q: A value is in A2 and the range A2:A10 is selected. Which shortcut copies A2 into A3:A10?
questions.solution: Ctrl+D (Fill Down) copies the top cell of the selection into the cells below it. Ctrl+R fills right, Ctrl+C only copies to the clipboard, and Ctrl+E is Flash Fill.

questions.q: Which part of the CPU performs subtraction and comparison operations?
questions.solution: Arithmetic (add, subtract) and logical (compare, AND/OR) operations are executed in the ALU. The program counter is a register holding the next instruction's address; the CU only coordinates.
questions.shortcut: Any verb like add/subtract/compare/AND-OR -> ALU, no matter how the question dresses it up.

questions.q: In a star topology, failure of the central hub/switch:
options: Has no effect on other nodes
Brings down communication between all nodes
Affects only the node next to the hub
Converts the network to a ring
questions.solution: Every node's cable meets at the central device, so its failure isolates the entire network - star's well-known single point of failure (individual cable breaks, however, affect only one node).
questions.shortcut: Centre dies, star dies - that weakness is the exam favourite.

questions.q: The tone of the author towards public libraries can best be described as:
questions.solution: The author calls the library 'the last indoor public space where no purchase is expected', documents its social services warmly, concedes budget problems honestly, and ends by demanding 'recognition' for an institution 'quietly succeeding in both worlds' — a clearly supportive tone with measured criticism of funding choices. Dismissive, mocking and indifferent all contradict the evaluative language of the closing paragraph.
questions.shortcut: Tone verdicts come from the closing lines: 'needs not nostalgia but recognition' is advocacy ⇒ supportive.
questions.passage:
There was a time when critics announced the death of the public library, confident that the internet had made buildings full of books redundant. The prediction has aged badly. Borrowing of printed books may have dipped in some cities, but library buildings are busier than they were a generation ago — because they have quietly become something more than warehouses for novels. In towns where a cup of coffee costs more than many can spare, the library remains the last indoor public space where no purchase is expected and no one asks you to leave.

Walk into any well-run city library this afternoon and you will find schoolchildren finishing homework at long tables, an unemployed man drafting job applications with a librarian's help, an elderly widow reading newspapers she cannot afford to subscribe to, and a coding club teaching teenagers in a side room. Librarians now spend as much time helping residents access government forms and digital services as they do recommending books.

This evolution has not been painless. Budgets trimmed by municipal councils force difficult choices between opening hours and new acquisitions, and smaller branches in poorer neighbourhoods — precisely those that need them most — are often the first to be marked for closure. Yet the case for investment has rarely been stronger. A society that worries about loneliness, digital exclusion and unequal schooling already owns an institution that addresses all three, staffed by professionals trained to help. The library needs not nostalgia but recognition: it is not a relic of the print age barely surviving; it is one of the few public institutions succeeding in both worlds.

questions.q:
Choose the correct order of the parts to make a meaningful sentence.

**1.** The old bridge was declared unsafe last month. **P:** Engineers examined every pillar for a week. **Q:** Traffic was diverted to a longer route. **R:** Repairs began within a fortnight. **S:** Commuters faced long delays at first. **6.** The bridge reopened, stronger than before.
questions.solution: Inspection first (**P**) → diversion (**Q**) → commuters' delays (**S**, consequence of Q) → repairs (**R**) → reopening (**S6**). PQSR.
questions.shortcut: Delays are the child of diversion: Q before S; repairs precede reopening.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (2).
questions.solution: 'The couple rarely watch television ___ Sundays.' Sundays are days of the week, and days take **on**: on Sunday, on Sundays. *In* takes longer periods (in June), *at* takes clock points (at 8 p.m.), *within* takes a length of time.
questions.passage: Suresh delivers parcels by day and studies for the bank examination by night. He is not ashamed (1) ______ his timetable: thirty minutes of maths on the bus, an hour of English after dinner. His wife manages the accounts of a small jeweller, and the couple rarely watch television (2) ______ Sundays. Suresh has applied (3) ______ three banks so far and keeps a diary of every exam date. His friends laugh at the diary, but he says a man who cannot put (4) ______ small pleasures for a year does not deserve a big one.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Had she left home earlier, she ___ the flight.
questions.solution: The inverted 'Had she left' is a type-3 (unreal past) condition, so the result takes **would have caught**. 'Would catch' is type 2, 'will catch' is type 1, and 'had caught' has no would.
questions.shortcut: Had + subject + V3 ... would have + V3.

questions.q: The SI unit of magnetic flux is:
questions.solution: Magnetic **flux** is measured in **weber (Wb)**. **Tesla** is the unit of magnetic field (flux density), **henry** is inductance and **gauss** is a CGS unit of field.

questions.q: Who became the first woman Director-General of the Geological Survey of India (GSI)?
questions.solution: **Varsha Ashok Aglawe** took over as the first woman DG of GSI on 31 July 2026.

questions.q: The **Sun Temple at Konark** was built by —
questions.solution: The Eastern Ganga king **Narasimhadeva I** built Konark in the 13th century as a giant chariot of the Sun god with 24 wheels. Anantavarman Chodaganga built the Jagannath temple at Puri; Kharavela is linked with the Hathigumpha inscription.

questions.q: Which franchise won the IPL 2026 title?
questions.solution: RCB beat Gujarat Titans by 5 wickets in the final (31 May 2026, Ahmedabad), defending their 2025 title — the first franchise to win the IPL and WPL in the same year.
questions.shortcut: RCB = back-to-back 2025 & 2026; GT was the beaten finalist.

questions.q: A milkman mixes 1 litre of water with every 5 litres of milk and sells the mixture at the cost price of milk. His profit per cent is:
questions.solution: Profit $= \frac{\text{water}}{\text{milk}} \times 100 = \frac{1}{5} \times 100 = 20\%$.
questions.shortcut: Free water per honest litre = profit fraction ⇒ 20%.

questions.q: A's income is 20% more than B's income. B's income is less than A's income by:
questions.solution:
Let B = 100, then A = 120.
B is short of A by 20 on base 120 ⇒ $\frac{20}{120} \times 100 = 16\frac{2}{3}\%$.

questions.q: Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 7. If their difference is 12, their sum is:
Which of the following is a rational number?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{8} \times \sqrt{2} = \sqrt{16} = 4$, which is rational. $\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}$, $2\pi$ and $\sqrt{5} - 1$ are all irrational.
questions.shortcut: Simplify each option first; only the one that becomes a perfect square root is rational.

questions.q:
Find the missing number:

**15   7   8**

**20   9   11**

**18   5   ?**
questions.solution: Third = first − second: 15 − 7 = 8 ✓, 20 − 9 = 11 ✓. So 18 − 5 = **13**. (23 adds instead.)
questions.shortcut: Output smaller than the first input → subtraction.

questions.solution: Border places numbered clockwise from the top-left corner (0-7). The cross-shaped mark is at 0, 1, 2, 3 (one step clockwise each time) and **alternates** between × and + (×, +, ×, +) → next: place 4 (bottom-right corner) as **×**. The dot is at 5, 6, 7, 0 (one step clockwise) → next place **1** (top-middle). The answer has × at the bottom-right corner and the dot at the top-middle.

questions.q: **A man walks 4 km North and 3 km East from his house while his wife stays at home. In which direction is the man from his wife?**
questions.solution: The man is at (3 E, 4 N) from home. Both components positive → **North-East** of his wife.
questions.shortcut: One person fixed = origin; read the compass word of the walker's coordinates.

questions.q:
Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out.

**345, 453, 534, 546**
questions.solution: Digit sums: 3+4+5 = 12, 4+5+3 = 12, 5+3+4 = 12, 5+4+6 = **15**. (The first three also use the same digits 3, 4, 5.) → **546**.
questions.shortcut: Same three digits shuffled in three options - the fourth uses a new digit.
